articles.title_orig: For Netanyahu, losing power could mean losing key shield in corruption trial
articles.title_zh: For Netanyahu, losing power could mean losing key shield in corruption trial
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his family will likely be questioned over corruption allegations sometime later this month, Israeli media reported Thursday.
According to the Times of Israel news website, Israeli police have asked the attorney-general for permission to question Netanyahu and his wife Sara -- and, possibly, his son Yair -- before the Jewish Passover holiday, which will begin March 30.
The expected questioning comes within the context of an ongoing corruption probe involving the Bezeq telecommunication company.
The case involves accusations that Bezeq owner Shaul Elovitch had instructed the Walla news website, which he owns, to provide Netanyahu with positive media coverage.
Last month, Israeli police recommended that Netanyahu be indicted for alleged corruption, saying there was now sufficient evidence to formally charge him in two separate graft cases.
The first case involves Israeli Hollywood producer Arnon Milchan, who was allegedly asked to purchase luxury items for Netanyahu and his wife.
The second relates to an alleged deal -- again for favorable media coverage -- with Arnon Mozes, publisher of Hebrew-language daily Yedioth Ahronoth.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump pushes board
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump pushes board
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO , effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.
The board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk."
President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard."
Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang.
Shares of Nvidia surged 33% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6.
"I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process."
Senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That update prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people said.
Huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people said. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations.
Trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump said the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy."
He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."
"On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote.
Several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk , CEO of SpaceX , Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected."
Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
For weeks following Huang's ouster, the company's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether company secrets or national security were compromised. The board said Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it."
"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company."
Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China.
Lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips.
"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., said in a statement Monday.
Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his plans to testify.
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., said Monday that Huang will publicly testify on Dec. 3 as the sole witness during a hearing titled, "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls."
"Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., a member of the Banking Committee, wrote in a post on X on Monday.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Dow Surges As Trump Says This On Huang's Nvidia Return; Chip Plays Rocket (Live Coverage)
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Dow Surges As Trump Says This On Huang's Nvidia Return; Chip Plays Rocket (Live Coverage)
articles.content_orig:
The major averages of U.S. equities surged on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, giving investors some hope that the relentless selling pressure seen last week may subside — at least temporarily.
The relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average , S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory . The S&P alone tumbled more than 9% after Huang's departure from the chipmaker was initially announced on Nov. 12 through Friday.
That sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts. But key questions linger around Nvidia and the artificial intelligence trade that has carried the bull market.
"I think the AI trade is back on," said Mark Gibbens, founder of Gibbens Capital Management. "I certainly believe this establishes a bottom and a floor in the AI trade and the recent market weakness."
He added that the news likely doesn't alleviate all concerns that have driven recent declines, including worries about data center approvals after the midterms and fears that the capital expenditures cycle may have peaked . But Gibbens thinks the "keystone" role that Nvidia plays in both financing the AI buildout and the technology's supply chain means a more stable picture of the chipmaker creates a brighter view of the overall market than before.
An encouraging sign that the correction may be over came even before Nvidia's Monday announcement, according to Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management. He said Friday's selling, which was indiscriminate and affected sectors beyond just AI-exposed companies, showed a bottom may have been building.
"Sometimes you just hit that crescendo where you know the market gets oversold, and I would argue that we'd be higher today, even without the Nvidia news," he said. Indeed, futures tied to the major stock indexes were broadly higher on Sunday night, before any news regarding Huang's return. "So I think that sort of signals we've likely found a place where we priced in, at least the near term, as much of the bad news that was giving markets jitters over the course of the last several weeks."
Strengthening the case for a bottom was that the technology sector's forward earnings valuation was cheaper than that of consumer staples, Hogan said. The S&P 500 consumer staples sector trades at a 20.5 multiple, per FactSet. Tech, meanwhile, trades at 16.3 times forward earnings. Hogan said that discrepancy doesn't square with the earnings outlook for the former sector.
Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, said Huang's return created a relief rally for a market that was oversold. But he's not sure the headline alone can get the market out of its funk.
"I think the rally will probably fizzle out because now people will pull back and still have the same questions we had before he was replaced," Woods said. Those questions will likely play out in congressional hearings , he speculated. "The market needed this jolt to get us back on our feet, but it is still a counter trend rally in an otherwise near-term downtrend."
Woods, though, said that the lows for the year are likely in, thanks to Friday's wash-out that spread to all sectors beyond those dependent on Nvidia's role in AI.
While investors celebrated Huang's return, the sell-off that accelerated after his departure started before worries about his position even began. That stemmed from concerns about financing the buildout , data center approvals after Democratic wins in the midterm elections and worries that hyperscaler capex may have already peaked or is about to.
That's why Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, is still nervous about the " picks and shovels " companies involved in the AI trade, a group he says includes Nvidia.
"We should enjoy this rally, and maybe it lasts a bit, but I think that picks and shovels trade is going to be solely dependent on what that rate of capex spend is going to be," he said. "That, at the end of the day, is the story that those companies are going to have to deal with outside of bounces like we're seeing now."
Traders at Goldman Sachs put it more succinctly.
"Not sure yet whether good or bad that the fate of the market is almost equal to the fate of one person. But hey ... We are not picky here," they said.
— CNBC's Michelle Fox and Deena Zaidi contributed reporting

articles.title_orig: States sue Musk companies over flood of sexualized images made with AI chatbot Grok
articles.title_zh: States sue Musk companies over flood of sexualized images made with AI chatbot Grok
articles.content_orig:

Elon Musk ’s SpaceX Super Intelligence Corp has been accused of profiting off its AI model Grok that produces child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual sexual images from photographs while failing to put safeguards in place to stop it.
Virginia and Oregon sued the company after several state attorneys general had announced investigations into Grok over similar claims in recent months.
The choices that went into building Grok led to a proliferation of child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual intimate imagery on the companies' platforms, the lawsuit alleges.
The companies prioritized their business model over the safety of millions of people, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in his state’s lawsuit.
“To push its lagging product, Grok, to tens of millions of new users, it stripped out industry-standard safeguards and marketed a ‘spicy mode’ built to produce nudity," Jones said in the lawsuit. “For these Defendants, weak safeguards were not a failure but a feature.”
Oregon also filed a lawsuit Monday. The attorneys general brought their separate but similar cases under their states' consumer protection statutes.
The lawsuits named as defendants several Musk companies and subsidiaries, including SpaceX, the social platform X, and SpaceX Super Intelligence, or SpaceXSI, the AI subsidiary of SpaceX.
In a statement, SpaceXSI said sexual content involving minors “whether real or AI-generated, is abhorrent. It has no place on X or in Grok, and neither do explicit images of real people made without their consent.”
The company said it had acted promptly to tighten protections when “bad actors” found ways to misuse Grok's image- and video-generation tool. If users try to break its safeguards to generate nonconsensual content, the company said, it takes “appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement.”
“Attempting to create this material is a serious crime, and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors,” the statement said.
The lawsuits come at a time of growing concern about AI’s risks for children, from its impact on brain development to the unhealthy relationships many young people have formed with chatbots.
Grok, which can be accessed through Musk's social media platform X, rolled out image generation and editing features to all users in December 2025, according to the Virginia lawsuit. By January, the tool had sparked a global backlash after it became clear Grok users could create realistic-looking but fake sexualized images of people. Researchers warned that some appeared to depict children.
As the Virginia lawsuit put it, “X was flooded with sexualized content — primarily of women.”
At least two countries, Malaysia and Indonesia, announced temporary bans and other nations said they were launching or widening investigations. In response, Grok prevented non-paying users from generating or editing images.
The change didn't stop users from making more non-consensual sexualized images; “it simply made that generation profitable," Virginia’s lawsuit said.
The developer of Grok, which was then known as xAI, has since rebranded as SpaceX Super Intelligence.
Virginia argued that most major AI developers designed their products so they could not be used to produce sexualized images to avoid the generation of nonconsensual content.
“Defendants declined to implement these safeguards. Defendants’ published system prompt materials — the set of instructions that guides the AI model’s behavior — told Grok to ‘assume good intent,’ stated that terms such as ‘teenage’ or ‘girl’ do not necessarily imply underage, and imposed minimal restrictions on sexual content," the lawsuit said.
The lawsuit noted that xAI marketed Grok from the outset as a tool that would “answer spicy questions that are rejected by most other AI systems.”
And it argued X made “false, deceptive or misleading” statements in January about changes intended to prevent Grok from allowing users to edit images of real people in revealing clothes.
Users could still create nonconsensual sexualized imagery through a standalone app and website, the lawsuit said. And when users openly traded “jailbreak” prompts to get around what limits Grok did have on sexualized images, Musk’s companies failed to promptly address the exploits, the Virginia lawsuit alleged.
Both lawsuits draw heavily on news outlets’ investigative reporting about the rollout of the tool, the backlash and the company’s response to it.
Virginia's lawsuit, filed in a state court in Richmond, argued that the Musk companies violated the state's consumer protection law by "misrepresenting that they implemented and enforced safeguards to protect consumers from exposure" to harmful sexualized imagery on their platforms.
It asked the court for $2,500 for each “willful violation” of the Virginia Consumer Protection Act, with an exact number to be proven at trial.
It also asked a judge to prevent the companies from further violating the consumer protection laws and force the defendants to give up any “ill-gotten gains” acquired in connection with the alleged violations.
The Oregon lawsuit makes a similar request.
“When xAI allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it. Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable," Jones said in a statement.

articles.title_orig: What Jensen Huang’s return means for Trump and China
articles.title_zh: What Jensen Huang’s return means for Trump and China
articles.content_orig:
President Trump and high-profile business leaders applauded Nvidia's shock move to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday, less than two weeks after the billionaire entrepreneur's resignation from the chipmaker.
In a post on social media platform Truth Social on Monday, Mr. Trump cheered the board's move, calling it "an absolutely GREAT decision" that would benefit the U.S. economy.
Mr. Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had spoken to Nvidia's board members to encourage them to reinstate Huang. "We have to protect our geniuses, and he is certainly a genius," he told the media outlet.
SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, another prominent supporter of Huang's, said in a post on X that "The mistake has been corrected," referring to the Nvidia co-founder's Nov. 12 resignation following revelations that he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy.
Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair and apologized to his family. Huang also had a relationship with a subordinate at Nvidia, the New York Times reported last week, while Reuters reported that he had an intimate relationship with a second employee at the company.
Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones on Monday announced that Huang's "reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers." Last week, during a quarterly earnings call discussing Nvidia's latest financial results, Jones said the board had no intention of rehiring him.
Sam Altman, CEO of ChatGPT developer OpenAI, in which Nvidia has pledged to invest up to $100 billion , issued a one-word post on X on Monday. "Jensen!" he wrote.
For their part, investors also seem heartened by Huang's return. Nvidia's stock soared $39.80 per share, or 32%, on Monday, quickly adding more than $1 trillion to the company's market value.
Not everyone cheered Huang's return to the world's most valuable AI chipmaker. In a statement, Sen. Elizabeth Warren called the Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Huang "reckless." The Massachusetts Democrat also pressed Nvidia's board to offer more details on its decision to rehire Huang.
"Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk," she said.
Lawmakers have moved to strengthen controls around U.S. exports to restrict China from gaining remote access to the most powerful chips and chipmaking equipment. On Nov. 16, the U.S. Commerce Department issued a new rule to close a loophole to protect sensitive American technology.
"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain," Sen. Charles Schumer, a Democrat from New York, said in a social media post. "We'll also work on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries."
Sen. John Cornyn, a Texas Republican, also expressed concern on social media about Nvidia's decision to restore Huang, questioning the board's conclusion that rehiring him posed no national security risk.
In addition to existing license requirements for advanced semiconductors, the rule adds new license requirements for exporting, re-exporting or transferring advanced semiconductors to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore or Thailand. The department said such nations "present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion."
Despite Huang's resumption of his duties at Nvidia, the House Intelligence Committee plans to carry on with a closed-door hearing with the executive next week, sources told CBS News. Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter were also expected to appear before other congressional panels in early December to answer questions about the company's export practices, among other issues.
Huang has long lobbied for the federal government to allow Nvidia to sell its most powerful AI chips to China.

Apple makes some of the best tech in the world, including stylish iPads, powerful MacBooks and, of course, the ubiquitous iPhone. But as anyone who loves Apple products will know, that quality also comes with a premium price tag, which is why Black Friday deals are such a good opportunity to grab some killer deals.
Black Friday week is just getting started and there are big discounts on the Apple Watch, MacBook Neo, and AirPods Pro 3, with the latter coming it at just $149. Some carriers are also offering great deals that will get you a free iPhone 18 Pro. But it's not just about tech: you can also currently get an Apple TV subscription for just $7 per month, so you can catch up on all the streamer's best shows, like Widow's Bay and Slow Horses.
Stick with us all day and keep checking back to see what other offers we're tracking live!
iPhone 18 Pro: free w/ new line + unlimited @ T-Mobile T-Mobile is offering the iPhone 18 Pro for free when you open a new line and use three T-Mobile Picks. (T-Mobile's new data plans offer up to 3 Picks or free perks, such as DashPass by DoorDash or Netflix Standard. The number of Picks you get is based on the plan's price or how many phone lines are on your plan). In our iPhone 18 Pro review , we said its the best phone money can buy. The iPhone 18 Pro features a 6.3-inch OLED 120Hz display (2622 x 1206), A20 Pro chipset, and 256GB of storage. You also get a 48MP main, 48MP ultrawide, and 48MP telephoto lens w/ 4x zoom. The front camera is 18MP.
Here's a deal I didn't expect to see. The new iPad mini A20 Pro is $100 off. The new model sports a larger 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR Display (2316 x 1512), A20 Pro CPU, 24% smaller bezels than its predecessor, and better audio. You also get a 12MP camera on the front and back and Wi-Fi 7 support. The base models (128GB/256GB) boast a 5-core CPU with 2 super cores and 3 efficiency cores, whereas the 512GB model bumps it to a 6-core CPU with 2 super cores and 4 efficiency cores. This is the first time it's on sale.
The AirPods Pro 3 are the Apple earbuds to get with superior active noise canceling and improved sound. In our AirPods Pro 3 review we said the Editor's Choice buds deliver the upgrade iPhone users have been waiting for with longer battery life, stronger noise cancellation, and smart new features like Live Translation. Save $70 right now.
Apple Watch Series 12 delivers the most accurate heart rate sensing yet in a smartwatch alongside a suite of advanced health and fitness features. It's powered by Apple's new S11 chip, which enables new Audio Intelligence features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap.
The iPad (11th Gen) remains the best Apple tablet for most people. In our iPad 11 review , we said it has significantly improved performance thanks to its A16 chip, longer battery life, and a larger 128GB starting storage option; Save $50 right now.
It's not the newest model, but the llast-gen iPad mini 7 is still a great compact tablet that's now on sale for Black Friday with $150 off. In our iPad mini 7 review , we said delivers excellent performance and battery life while retaining its predecessor's vibrant display and portable design.
It's a minor discount, but we'll take it. The MacBook Neo sports a 13-inch Liquid Retina (2408 x 1506) display, A18 Pro chipset, 8GB of RAM, 256GB SSD, and 1080p FaceTime HD camera. There's also the option to add TouchID and a 512GB SSD for a total price of $699. The 2.7-lb. laptop is available in Indigo, Blush, Citrus, and Silver. In our MacBook Neo review , we said no other laptop comes close in terms of bang for your buck.
The 13-inch MacBook Air M4 features the same elegant design as its predecessors, along with excellent M4-driven performance and epic battery life. This starting configuration comes with 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD. Right now you can get $250 off, which is a great discount.
Now that all of Apple's latest iPhones and Macs ship with Wi-Fi 7 support, it's probably a good time to update your Wi-Fi router if you haven't already. Especially since I don't think Apple is bringing back its AirPort routers anytime soon.
After testing many of the best mesh routers, I can easily say that using one of Amazon's own Eero mesh kits feels as close as you can get to Apple router. Not only are they easy to set up and use, Eero's routers really give you that "it just works" feeling you've come to expect from Apple devices.
Right now, you can pick up the Eero Pro 7 in a three-pack for $599 at Amazon . Alternatively, if you live somewhere smaller, you can get a two-pack for just $399 . In our Eero Pro 7 review , we loved how compact these new mesh devices are and the fact that they ship with two, high-speed 5 Gigabit Ethernet ports around back.
If you're looking for one of the best all-in-one computers, you can't go wrong with Apple's iMac. Right now, you can get the new iMac M6 for $86 off at Amazon . However, if you want to save even more, the iMac M4 is down to $1,199 or $300 off its normal price.
While Apple's silver iMac M4 is discounted the most right now, you can also get $100 off the blue model too. Though I haven't tried the iMac M4, in my iMac M6 review I praised its speedy performance and the fact that it now ships with Apple's proprietary N1 networking chip which adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0 support.
If you’ve been using a Mac for some time, then you’ve likely heard of Satechi. For those who haven’t though, the company makes Apple accessories that look and feel like they were made by Cupertino itself. I’ve used their Hub & Stand with my Mac mini as well as their mechanical keyboards and both haven't let me down yet. Right now, you can pick up Satechi's 6-in-2 USB-C Snap Hub, OntheGo 5-in-1 USB-C Hub and Slim EX Wireless Mouse all at a discounted price. They're also available in Blush, Citrus, Indigo and Silver to match whatever MacBook Neo finish you have. In fact, our own Paul Antill tried them out with his MacBook Neo and was throughly impressed.
The Mac mini M4 was a breath of fresh air with its completely redesigned case. However, the Mac mini M6 takes things up a notch by turbocharging its internals with Apple's more powerful M6 chip. It's also the first Mac mini ever to have the company's proprietary N1 networking chip which adds support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0. Right now, you can grab the base model of the Mac mini M6 for just $779 at Amazon which is $120 off its regular price. I reviewed the upgraded model with 24GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage and good news, it's also on sale for $1,199 or $100 off. If you do any serious photo or video editing or even want to run AI models locally, I'd recommend this upgraded version over the base model. Likewise, it will last you even longer, though the base model should work well for most workloads for years to come too.
My colleague Will wrote about this deal before, but it's such an epic deal I just wanted to flag it again. Amazon is taking $100 off the Apple Watch 12. My wife got me one for my birthday this past October and I love it. (I upgraded from an Apple Watch 8).

articles.title_orig: Amazon’s China-made adult bed rails recalled after 89-year-old woman dies of suffocation
articles.title_zh: Amazon’s China-made adult bed rails recalled after 89-year-old woman dies of suffocation
articles.content_orig:
Thousands of adult bed rails from China that were sold in the US have been recalled after an 89-year-old woman died of suffocation when she was trapped between the product and her mattress.
About 2,114 adult bed rails sold on Amazon by Guangzhou Yupin Technology Co. – a Chinese company doing business as Xentrawave – are included in the recall, according to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission.
All batches of Xentrawave’s model XT016 and batch number 20251212 of model XT026 are included in the recall for failing to meet mandatory safety requirements, because customers can be pinned between the rail and the side of the mattress – posing a risk of death by asphyxiation.
The XT106 model adult bed rail also doesn’t meet structural stability requirements and its push pins and push pin holes are incorrectly sized, posing a risk of laceration, the agency said.
The CPSC said it has received one report of a death related to the Xentrawave recall, involving the 89-year-old woman who died from asphyxiation.
Customers can find the model numbers XT016 or XT026 on the front of the product’s outer packaging and the first page of the instruction manual.
For the XT026 model, consumers can locate the batch number on the product label attached to the back of the bed rail’s gray fabric pouch and in the instruction manual.
Consumers should immediately stop use of the recalled bed rails and contact Xentrawave for a full refund.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
They will be asked to cut the foam padding on the bed rail handles, disassemble the product and email a photo of the destroyed bed rail to xentrawavedirect@163.com or submit it online at https://xentrawahelp.com/xentrawave-bed-rail-safety-recall/ .
The recalled XT016 bed rails were sold on Amazon from May 2025 through March 2026 and the XT026 model was sold from March 2026 through August 2026. The bed rails cost between $37 and $40.
The bed rails were manufactured by China-based Guangzhou Nanyu Medical Technology Co.

articles.title_zh: Nasdaq roars back by 6% as Nvidia soars on Huang’s return, S&P 500 rebounds 4%: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
U.S. equities surged on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, reviving the artificial intelligence trade and pushing major indexes higher after all three major market averages ended Friday in a correction.
The S&P 500 added 4.6%, and the Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1,434 points, or 3%. Each of the three major averages is on pace for its best day since April 2025.
Nvidia soared 31% after the company's board returned Huang as the head of the company , effective immediately. Huang had resigned earlier this month after reportedly engaging in a number of extramarital affairs, one of which was with an alleged Chinese spy.
President Donald Trump applauded the move and told CNBC that Huang "did nothing wrong." The president also said that he spoke with Nvidia's board and "convinced" them to reinstate him.
"He had bad judgment having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents, but he did nothing wrong other than he created a chip that's invaluable, many chips that are invaluable," he told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a " Squawk on the Street " interview.
Other stocks in the AI trade jumped in sympathy with Nvidia on Monday. Micron Technology added 19%, while CoreWeave skyrocketed 20%. Advanced Micro Devices was up 6%. "Magnificent Seven" members Alphabet and Meta Platforms popped 6% each, and Microsoft gained 2%.
"Jensen Huang's return restores and rebuilds confidence in the AI ecosystem: its major suppliers, its core building blocks, and its demand outlook," said Hendi Susanto, portfolio manager and research analyst at Gabelli Funds.
To be sure, the trade "still has to push through a lot of noise about financing, geopolitics, durability and skepticism, even though companies across the AI supply chain keep reporting strong demand," Susanto added.
The moves mark a massive turnaround for the tech sector following last week's sell-off , as worries about the AI trade continued to spook investors despite Anthropic's record debut on Thursday. Trump told CNBC Monday that the recent turmoil likely had an impact on his decision to call for Huang's return.
By the end of last week — the worst weekly decline for the Nasdaq and Dow in more than six years, and the largest for the S&P 500 since April 2025 — all three of the major averages were in a correction, down 10% from their recent highs, and the Nasdaq was lower for the year.
The Nasdaq-100 index ended Friday close to a bear market, down almost 20% from its latest high.
Investors this week will get a breather, no matter what price action looks like. Markets are closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday, and Friday's session will be shortened with the closing bell set to ring at 1 p.m. ET.
Nvidia reinstated former CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, leading several Wall Street analysts to turn more bullish on the stock.
CNBC Pro subscribers can read more about what analysts had to say here .
The massive sell-off seen on Friday may have created an opportunity for investors, as the S&P 500 was "oversold" after moving into correction territory, according to BTIG.
"While we still don't have the full-fledged breadth washout, with the SPX breaking 7k, and a host of capitulatory signals firing, this is at least a pitch we are willing to swing at," said Jonathan Krinsky, the firm's chief market technician, in a note dated Sunday.
However, Krinsky added that he still doesn't think Friday's tumble is the "final low," saying that "we are looking for a short-term rally back towards 7250-7350 before likely turning lower again."
The broad market index was last trading around 7,250 with its roughly 5% rise in afternoon trading on Monday.
Check out CNBC's live blog here to read more about the stocks making big moves.

President Donald Trump told CNBC's " Squawk on the Street " that he had to get involved in reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia "for the country."
"I better get involved. If I didn't get involved, you probably have a a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come," Trump said.
Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview that he made the deal with the company's board to have Huang back. Huang had an alleged affair with a Chinese spy, along with two reported affairs with Nvidia employees. He had initially resigned from the company on Nov. 12.
When asked about how to convince Republicans who are concerned about Huang's return, Trump said he will speak to his party.
"When I speak to them, they're going to be great," Trump said.
The return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has removed a major source of uncertainty and restored the "visionary leadership" that helped build the artificial intelligence infrastructure ecosystem, said David Miller, chief investment officer and portfolio manager at Catalyst funds.
"[H]is reinstatement could serve as a catalyst for a much broader recovery in AI related stocks," he said. "While questions remain about the ultimate returns on massive AI capital expenditures, today's announcement meaningfully improves sentiment and reduces a major risk that had been hanging over the sector."
Investment bank Barclays thinks the recent AI sell-off could be "going too far."
The "prevailing bear thesis," according to Venu Krishna at Barclays, is that AI growth is running into fundamental roadblocks that could risk a "broader macro shock."
Krishna is taking a more measured position, however.
"We remain skeptical, and think valuations are already pricing in substantial adverse outcomes here," he said in a Monday note to clients.

articles.title_orig: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
articles.title_zh: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
articles.content_orig:
Gaza has been turned into "a toxic wasteland", with more than 99% of the Palestinian territory showing indicators of environmental contamination from Israeli military attacks, a new report from the charity Oxfam says .
Heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and dioxins and biological contaminants are threats to Palestinians now and potentially for decades to come, it says.
Oxfam International's executive director, Amitabh Behar, said the impact on Gaza "will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival".
In response, the Israeli embassy in the UK said the report "falls short of professional standards".
Behar also accused Israel of "environmental war crimes" as part of an "ongoing genocide in Gaza".
Israel has rejected genocide accusations in an ongoing case at the International Court of Justice as baseless and distorted. It maintains that its military campaign in Gaza is an act of self-defence against Hamas in response to the group's deadly attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, and that it takes steps to mitigate civilian harm.
Oxfam and the UK-based Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS) used satellite imagery, remote sensing, spatial analysis and other open-source data to draw their conclusions in the most comprehensive report to date on the severe environmental impacts caused by three years of intense war in Gaza.
The report details how munitions used in Israel's intense bombardment, as well as the debris from destroyed buildings and infrastructure, all have an impact on the environment. In February, a UN special rapporteur stated that more than 200,000 tonnes of explosives were dropped on Gaza in almost two years - "the equivalent of the total energy of approximately 13 Hiroshima-type nuclear bombs".
Last year, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) estimated that Israel's military operations destroying homes and infrastructure had generated more than 61 million tonnes of debris across the territory, with about 15% potentially carrying a high risk of contamination from hazardous materials.
"There are going to be chronic health impacts that are long term because a lot of these contaminants are persistent in the environment," Oxfam report author Lama Abdul Samad told the BBC.
She says that now and in future Gazans are likely to suffer from increased respiratory diseases, cancers, organ damage and a rise in birth defects and stillbirths.
With all six wastewater treatment plants out of operation in Gaza, untreated sewage currently makes its way into groundwater and the Mediterranean Sea. The health impact has recently been exacerbated by heavy winter storms causing rainwater to mix with wastewater and flow through streets and tent sites housing displaced people.
Testing types and levels of contamination is often not possible because Gazan laboratories have been destroyed and there are Israeli restrictions on the entry of specialist testing equipment and scientists. The BBC has approached the Israeli military for comment.
UNEP said security concerns also prevented its expert staff from previously travelling to Gaza.
The Oxfam report calls for a full, independent environmental assessment to be carried out in Gaza to identify contamination risks ahead of a clean-up. It says special attention must be given to the protection of workers involved.
The Israeli embassy sharply criticised the report, arguing that it relied on satellite imagery "and unverified assumptions, and its methodology lacks the academic rigour needed to withstand serious scrutiny".
It said the report drew conclusions about Gaza's soil and groundwater without considering the excavation of hundreds of kilometres of tunnels by Hamas, rendering it fundamentally flawed.
Already, Gazan doctors have been reporting increased acute respiratory infections caused by dust and pollution from destroyed buildings and displaced people burning plastic, rags and cardboard to keep warm and cook food. Gastrointestinal diseases are linked to unsafe water and poor sanitation.
A Palestinian dermatologist, Dr Alaa Abu Hajar, told the BBC he had seen a five-fold increase in chronic skin diseases since the start of the war, putting this down to environmental pollution and overcrowded, unhygienic living conditions in tents and displacement camps.
"There are rodents, rubbish and sewage that's spread through the streets," he says. "Unfortunately, the age group most affected is children."
Farmers and those working in fishing say that pollution of the soil and sea mean they are unable to produce food that is safe.
"Sewage and wastewater are discharged into the sea without treatment and this is a great disaster," complains fisherman Abu al-Abed Sultan. "There is also rubble from destroyed houses that's dumped into the sea. When we lower our nets, we catch rubble and garbage. This harms the marine environment; the fish are affected and so are the fishermen."
At least 74,746 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the war in Gaza, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. The UN says that humanitarian conditions remain dire.
Israel has conditioned large-scale Gaza reconstruction on the full disarmament of Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups. In July, Hamas accepted a plan put forward by the US-led Board of Peace to give up its weapons in exchange for an Israeli troop withdrawal. However, the Israeli government said the proposal was insufficient.

And there's been some genuinely great savings in the worlds of hi-fi and home cinema already. Whether you're after a pair of budget Bluetooth headphones or a premium OLED TV, there's plenty of discounts to choose from.
And if you're not sure what to choose, that's where we come in. Our team of expert reviewers have tried and tested hundreds of hi-fi and home cinema products to find the very best.
Every deal below, unless flagged, features a product that has been reviewed and recommended by our testers, and is at a genuinely excellent price. We only recommend products that have four stars or more, and the best of the best will also have won a prestigious What Hi-Fi? Award.
We'll be here all week sharing deals and advice. And we're starting strong this Monday – take a look for yourself...
I’ve covered more Prime Days, Black Fridays and general AV sale events than I care to count. This, plus my experience as What Hi-Fi?’s editor-in-chief and a regular reviewer, gives me an expert knowledge of the market as a whole, which is why I’ll occasionally be chipping in here, offering my two cents on the top savings to jump at, and ones to avoid.
As the Deals Writer for What Hi-Fi?, I spend my days covering deals on all the latest TVs, soundbars, projectors, amps, speakers, headphones and more. I’ve spent years taking part in Black Friday both as a writer and a consumer, and know how important it is to cut through the noise to recommend the best value products. This week I’ll be constantly searching for new lowest prices and for ways to help our readers save money, but also making sure we’re highlighting products that are genuinely worth your money and have earned a recommendation from our rigorous review process.

I love high-end gear, of course, but I also firmly believe that great picture and sound quality should be available to all. The good news is that you really don’t have to spend a fortune to get a home cinema experience to be proud of – especially if you shop around. I’m always on the hunt for big discounts, and Black Friday often unearths some great deals, but not all offers are as great as they might at first seem. Over the next few days, I will be flagging the real deals and warning you off the fake ones.
I run our hi-fi and audio section, and have spent over 14 years at What Hi-Fi? reviewing everything from premium turntables and stereo amplifiers to affordable DACs and speakers. Armed with plenty of advice, experience, and a desire to ensure everyone gets the ideal product for their needs and system, I will be able to tell you whether a Black Friday hi-fi deal is worth the plunge or not – and recommend better alternatives for better value.

Abhijeet Mishra / SamMobile
Now Bar live notifications
Samsung is moving its Now Bar live notifications closer to Apple's Dynamic Island, with changes to both their position and the way you switch between ongoing activities. We've tested the new layout in early Galaxy S27 series software.
Samsung is working on a new look for the Now Bar's live notifications, and the resemblance to Apple's Dynamic Island is hard to miss. We've exclusively discovered the changes in early Galaxy S27 series software, offering a glimpse of how Samsung could present ongoing activities in a future update.
On current versions of One UI, the live notification pill sits beside the clock on the left. Samsung's new layout moves it to the top center, in the area around the front camera.
The timer countdown, Torch indicator, and expandable activity controls you see here are familiar features already in One UI. The new layout displays those existing updates from this central position.
Centered torch Now Bar pill
Centered timer Now Bar pill
Samsung is also changing how you switch between compact live notification pills. Currently, you swipe up and down to move between ongoing activities. In the version we tested, you swipe left and right instead, without first expanding the pill.
That sideways switching gesture, combined with the placement around the selfie camera, gives Samsung's existing live notifications a more Dynamic Island-like feel.
Now Bar settings also include a Moment effects page, with Sports as the only listed download. It offers celebrations for your favorite teams' scores and wins in selected sports supported by Google Sports.
Samsung has already introduced sports animations in the One UI 9.5 beta . The broader Moment effects name could leave room for other types of effects later, but additional categories haven't been confirmed.
All of these changes are still under development and could be revised before Samsung brings them to Galaxy devices. They will likely debut with the Galaxy S27 series before reaching existing devices through the One UI 9.5 update .

JPMorgan said the acquisition could broaden CrowdStrike's security platform amid vendor consolidation, adding network security capabilities to better address growing demand for AI sovereignty. CrowdStrike and Zscaler announced a definitive all-stock agreement Monday, valuing Zscaler at approximately $43.9 billion in enterprise value, based on CrowdStrike's November 20 closing share price.
JPMorgan analyst Brian Essex said CrowdStrike remains well-positioned to secure AI through a platform spanning runtime, identity, and data. He also said the company could report another quarter of accelerating annual recurring revenue growth.
The firm raised its price target on CRWD stock to $240 from $235, maintaining an 'Overweight' rating.
According to Citizens, the CrowdStrike-Zscaler combination could boost demand for cybersecurity assets, positioning SentinelOne as an attractive strategic target given its endpoint distribution, AI security capabilities, and autonomous SOC, per TheFly. It raised the price target on S stock to $28 from $25, maintaining an 'Outperform' rating.
Meanwhile, Oppenheimer analyst Ittai Kidron said the combination would bring together CrowdStrike's (CRWD) ability to detect and secure devices with Zscaler's (ZS) cloud-based network security, enabling suspicious endpoint activity to trigger restrictions on access and data movement.
The firm said shared security data could support a unified investigation and response process that neither company currently offers independently. The deal could pressure Fortinet (FTNT) and Check Point (CHKP) to accelerate mergers and acquisitions, the note said, identifying Netskope (NTSK) and SentinelOne (S) as attractive potential targets.
CrowdStrike reported fiscal third-quarter (Q3) revenue of $1.58 billion, exceeding analyst estimates of $1.53 billion, according to Koyfin data. For the fourth quarter, the company expects revenue of $1.638 billion to $1.644 billion and adjusted net income between $380.3 million and $383 million.
The management said it expects the Zscaler transaction to be immediately accretive to free cash flow per share upon closing, before synergies. It also expects the acquisition to be accretive to revenue growth, non-GAAP operating margin and free cash flow margin after synergies within the first fiscal year following closing.
Following the earnings report, Barclays analyst Saket Kalia raised CRWD's price target to $265 from $235 and maintained an 'Overweight' rating on the shares. Channel checks show further strength in Falcon Flex, the analyst said in its note, according to TheFly.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around CrowdStrike (CRWD) and Check Point (CHKP) was 'bullish', while SentinelOne (S) and Netskope (NTSK) attracted 'extremely bullish' sentiment. Meanwhile, sentiment around Fortinet (FTNT) remained 'neutral'.
Cybersecurity stocks have delivered mixed performances this year. Meanwhile, Zscaler (ZS) and Check Point (CHKP) have declined over 11% and 14%, respectively. In comparison, the First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR) has gained 28.3%, while the Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) has risen more than 51% year-to-date.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya
articles.title_zh: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya
articles.content_orig:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday lauded an "exemplary" military operation that sank one of Russia's newest ships at a Libyan port, after Kyiv's forces struck their target with several domestically made naval drones.
The incident followed a suspected Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and occurred less than a week after damage was inflicted on Russian President Vladimir Putin 's prized Crimea bridge.
In a social media post , Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces deployed seven sea drones to attack the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, at Benghazi's port in the early hours of Sunday morning. Ukraine's president posted dramatic video footage showing Ukraine's naval drones triggering a massive explosion on the Russian ship.
"Despite all the enemy's efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk. It's one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war," Zelenskyy said. "We continue our operations in designated waters," he added.
Satellite imagery taken on Sunday showed the Merkury mostly underwater, having capsized
The Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons, was hit by Ukrainian forces. A Ka-27 military helicopter on the Merkury was also destroyed.
Asked about reports of attacks on Russian ships off the coast of Libya, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said information on this would be provided via the Defense Ministry.
The Security Service of Ukraine, the SBU, said Monday that the attacks "once again demonstrated that the Russian military fleet and its logistics have no safe routes even far beyond the Black Sea," according to a Google translation.
"Such unique special operations destroy the enemy's logistical capabilities and force Russia to pay for aggression even at a strategic distance from Ukraine," the SBU said via Telegram.
The United Nations Support Mission in Libya, or UNSMIL, expressed "serious concern" over the drone attacks in a statement saying the country "cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts."
"UNSMIL calls for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation to establish the facts and hold those responsible to account," it added.
The incident is not the first time Libya has seen attacks linked to the Russia-Ukraine war near its territory.
In March, Moscow's Transport Ministry accused Ukraine of striking the Arctic Metagaz, a liquefied natural gas tanker, as part of a suspected sea drone attack in the Mediterranean between Libya and Malta.

articles.title_orig: Moscow accuses Estonia of hostile actions on 'verge of triggering open war'
articles.title_zh: Moscow accuses Estonia of hostile actions on 'verge of triggering open war'
articles.content_orig:
Russia has accused Estonia of carrying out numerous “hostile actions” and threatened “open war” against the neighbouring Baltic state.
Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday accused Tallinn of a ⁠⁠range of hostile actions, asserting that the NATO and European Union member state is “on ⁠⁠the verge of triggering open war”.
The outburst comes after Estonia announced the planned closure of its border with Russia, and a Ukrainian attack on a Russian ship in the Baltic Sea.
The ministry set out its accusations in a statement after ⁠⁠summoning Estonia’s charge d’affaires in Moscow, Marek Uhtegi, to issue a formal protest over Tallinn’s decision to close the border.
“The Estonian diplomat was once again told that such provocative and extremely dangerous actions are on the verge of triggering open war with Russia,” it said, adding that Estonia is displaying “Russophobic” tendencies.
Among a list of additional accusations, the ministry said Estonia had “tacitly allow[ed] its airspace to be used by Ukrainian drones for attacks on northwestern Russia”. Tallinn was swift to deny the claim.
It also accused Estonia of trying to obstruct the movement of Russian cargo ships in the Baltic Sea, banning the transit of Russian and Belarusian grain, seeking a ban on the Russian language and threatening to close the Russian Orthodox Church.
“The Russian side reserves the right to take comprehensive political and diplomatic measures aimed at protecting Russia’s national interests and the legitimate rights of its citizens,” the ministry said.
Estonia is host to a sizeable ethnic Russian population, which Moscow has often claimed is subject to discrimination.
Russia’s incursions into eastern Ukraine in 2014 were based on claims of suppression of Russian speakers’ rights in the region.
Earlier this month, Estonia said it would close border crossings with Russia from December 1 for at least six months, having accused the Kremlin’s security services of staging an attempted arson attack on an Estonian defence company.
This marked a sharp escalation in tensions between Estonia and Russia, which Tallinn – Kyiv’s ally – sees as part of a broader campaign of hostile activity linked to Moscow’s war in Ukraine.
Russia has denied any involvement in the attack. Closing the border, the ministry said, “will inevitably backfire – not only on Tallinn itself but also on its allies within the EU and NATO”.
In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Estonia did not respond to all of the allegations but denied that it allows its territory to be used for Ukrainian military operations.
“While we generally do not comment on or engage with Russian propaganda narratives, in this case we can reiterate that Estonia has never allowed, and will never allow, its territory to be used for military operations by another country,” it said.
“Other countries in our region have also made this position clear,” it added.
Russia has long accused Estonia and other NATO states in the Baltic region of allowing Ukrainian drones to use their airspace. Ukrainian drones have frequently entered NATO airspace, but Kyiv says this is a result of Russian signal jamming.
NATO countries have repeatedly denied intentionally allowing drones to use their airspace, and blamed Russia for the incursions.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, speaking in Berlin, said the alliance was monitoring the situation in Estonia, along with an incursion last week by Russian missiles into Poland, adding that NATO had options available to respond.
“We see situations in Poland and Estonia, etc ,” Rutte said. “When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary.”

articles.title_orig: Grand Theft Auto VI Leaker CYBERLEEK Posts the Xbox Build’s Executable, Calling It a Fight Against Subscriptions and $20 “Ultimate Editions”
articles.title_zh: Grand Theft Auto VI Leaker CYBERLEEK Posts the Xbox Build’s Executable, Calling It a Fight Against Subscriptions and $20 “Ultimate Editions”
articles.content_orig:
CYBERLEEK , the anonymous hacker/leaker (or group) responsible for the major pre-release Grand Theft Auto VI footage leaks, has now delivered on their final promise: posting the Xbox build's executable after already sharing the rest of the files, as an "early Christmas gift".
The document published alongside the release, available on Pastebin , says:
CYBERLEEK is about fighting anti-consumerism in the games industry. It was never about damaging the players. The players have no fault in any of this. That is why the ending was never leaked, and why the story mode was never spoiled. Millions waited years for this game, and ruining that experience would mean hurting exactly the people CYBERLEEK stands with. The enemy is the tactic, not the game: subscriptions bolted onto single-player games, 20-dollar "ultimate editions" that unlock what already sits in the game files, licenses sold as purchases. All of it needs to be eliminated.
"Untouchable" is supposed to be a word for billion dollar companies. This release says otherwise. Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has. The rules hold only as long as people obey them. This Grand Theft Auto VI build is what it looks like when someone does not.
What really matters for PC gamers, though, is that this could be the gateway to a playable build ahead of the official release. NotRexed , the same modder behind Hookshot (the native PC recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake ), was waiting just for the executable to go ahead with the Leonida project, a static recompilation project to get the Xbox Series version running on PC:
The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game .
Early. The game does not boot yet. Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer.
It should be noted that NotRexed had previously recompiled The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom , but that repository is nowhere to be found, likely because Nintendo nuked it. The same might very well befall the equivalent Grand Theft Auto VI project.
Still, the clock is ticking. We might get at least a demonstration of Rockstar's new masterpiece running natively on PC relatively soon. Meanwhile, the game continues to sell gangbusters on consoles , and Rockstar also just dropped The Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album (Deluxe Edition) .
About the author : With over two decades of experience in gaming journalism, Alessio Palumbo has led the gaming vertical at Wccftech since August 2015. He started working at a young age for Italian websites like Everyeye.it, Gamestar.it, Nextgame.it, and Multiplayer.it before kickstarting the indie English-language publication Worlds Factory as its founder and Editor in Chief. 

In the last decade, he has coordinated the overall output of Wccftech's gaming section, managed PR relations, assigned reviews, produced daily news coverage, edited gaming content as needed, and delivered game reviews.  

Arguably, his trademark content is the long series of exclusive developer interviews that have been cited by Wikipedia and by the biggest news media and gaming publications. 

His passion for technology also makes him knowledgeable when it comes to gaming hardware and tech. His favorite genres include RPGs, MMORPGs, and action/adventure games.

German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius urged calm over reports that Russia was planning to launch a nuclear-armed satellite into space as early as next month.
"First of ​all, ‌let's remain calm, because there are reports — that's true — but ‌it's ​not clear what kind of weapons these are, and the ​effect they might have depends, in ⁠turn, ​on where they ​are deployed," Pistorius told ​reporters in ‌Berlin.
"Therefore, it's too early to ​speculate ⁠publicly about this. We are consulting ⁠internally ​and taking the necessary measures."
German public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung first reported on the matter, which said that internal intelligence reports circulated among NATO countries earlier this month said that Russia was ready to bring the alleged satellite, named Sputnik-S, out of storage in Moscow.
The reports said Russia may be planning to launch it as soon as December.
Nuclear weapons are banned in orbit by the 1967 Outer Space Treaty , of which Moscow is a signatory.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said not allowing Ukraine into NATO in 2008 was a mistake.
At the 2008 summit in Bucharest, Romania , German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President Nicolas Sarkozy argued that they weren't ready to extend NATO membership to Ukraine.
US President George W. Bush said he was in favor of having Ukraine enter into NATO.
But both Germany and France said that that would hurt relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The NATO summit then decided that Ukraine would eventually join the alliance , but offered no timetable.
At a press conference on Monday, Merz was asked about whether he thinks the time was right to talk about Ukraine's membership in NATO.
To which Merz said, "If it [Ukraine] had become a member of NATO, this war could probably have been prevented."
Merz meant Russia's war against Ukraine when he said "this war" at the press conference after a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.
Angela Merkel defended her decision at the Bucharest summit as of 2024 as well, saying a large proportion of the Ukrainian population had opposed joining NATO at the time.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called on Russia to end its "dangerous provocations" after two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in Poland on Friday.
Merz delivered those remarks after having met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Berlin on Monday.
"Poland can count on our full solidarity. And if necessary, NATO will of course defend every inch of allied territory," Merz said.
Merz said Europe and NATO must strengthen their defenses.
Drones have repeatedly strayed into NATO airspace in the year since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
The incident also came at a time as Poland was hosting a two-week military exercise by Ukraine's allies.
German startup investments in fields such as robotics and defense are set to almost triple this year, a study noted on Monday.
The German Start-up Association and the Joachim Herz Foundation study predicted that investments in so-called "deep tech startups" will surge from just €2.9 billion ($3.17 billion) last year to 8.1 billion ($8.9 billion) this year.
The study described the rise as a "major success for Germany as a business location."
"Deep tech" typically refers to developing cutting-edge technologies based on scientific research, such as AI, biotechnology and quantum computing.
A handful of massive fundraising rounds by firms including humanoid robot developer Neura Robotics, AI drone maker Helsing and defense tech group Quantum Systems drove the investment boom.
The study also showed about 300 new deep tech startups are expected to be founded this year, a 40% rise compared with last year.
Newly found startups tend to be founded around economic hubs like Berlin and Hamburg, which are also home to leading universities and research institutes.
The study also highlighted challenges, including limited funding compared with their US counterparts and insufficient support to move startups from the laboratory to the real world.
Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools.
They said that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats.
More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning.
Similar reports have also emerged to the north of Germany, in Denmark .
As in Germany, Danish police said they did not believe the threats were credible, "but they understandably create insecurity locally at the schools."
Read more about the disruptive incidents that have targeted Europe in recent weeks.
Germany's Freie Wähler (Free Voters) party have chosen a new chairman, weeks after their former front man Hubert Aiwanger unexpectedly passed away on November 4.
The party announced on Monday that Bavaria's Digital Affairs Fabian Mehring is to succeed Aiwanger both as party leader on the federal level and as one of two co-chairs of the Bavaria section of they party. T he second state co-chair still needs to be decided.
Aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel room at the age of 55 with no foul play suspected. He's been the party's defining figure for almost four decades, having led the Free Voters to substantial success, especially in Bavaria .
The Free Voters are originally a grass roots party in Bavaria and sit on the conservative edge of the political spectrum. They've been in government in Bavaria as junior coaltion partners of the Christian Social Union (CSU) , sister party to Chancellor Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU).
There are also changes in the Bavarian state government. Tobias Gotthardt is to take over as economy minister, while Environment Minister Thorsten Glauber is set to become deputy premier behind Bavaria state Premier Markus Söder . The appointments still require formal approval by party conventions.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has inisted that NATO was ready to defend itself in the face of potential Russian threats against any of its member states.
"We will always defend every inch of our NATO territory," Wadephul said at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.
His comments come after three Russian projectiles violated Polish airspace on Friday and crashed in the southeast of the country.
Wadephul is attending the NATO assembly in Berlin and DW has a dedicated blog on those talks where you can read all about how Russia's war in Ukraine is taking center stage for the defense alliance.
A massive strike is underway in Germany hitting major car brands another manufacturing factors. Metal and electrical workers are demanding better pay ahead of upcoming wage talks later this week. The strike has been initiated by IG Metall, Germany’s biggest and most powerful union.
Famous car brands Mercedes and BMW were affected as was an Opel plant, which is part of the international Stellantis group.
The strikes began on Friday and are due to continue until Tuesday. Wage negotiations are then set to continue on Wednesday with another round of collective bargaining for some 3.7 million workers across the sector.
The union is demanding a pay rise of 5% over one year while the employers association, Gesamtmetall, has offered a one-time payment and a pay increase of 1.3%.
The tough struggle over wages comes as especially the German car industry is facing serious headwinds because of higher energy prices, US tariffs and mounting Chinese competition.

articles.title_orig: A ‘GTA 6’ Player Finds Tommy Vercetti’s Shirt And Portal To Original Vice City
articles.title_zh: A ‘GTA 6’ Player Finds Tommy Vercetti’s Shirt And Portal To Original Vice City
articles.content_orig:
Easter Egg Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA 6 GTA Vice City
Grand Theft Auto 6 is a big game filled with a lot of secrets, Easter eggs, mysteries, and more. And one of the most elaborate and well-hidden secrets in Rockstar’s new game has just been revealed by a YouTuber. It takes some time and involves going to 12 different spots across the map to hit buttons, but you’ll be rewarded with a trip back to the original Vice City and a classic shirt.
All credit for discovering and figuring out this wild secret must go to content creator Memeio, who found a tower in the southern part of the map that contained a button that, when pressed, played a small noise from GTA: Vice City. I also found this tower while reviewing the game, but didn’t think to go hunting down a bigger secret. Memeio did, and after a few days of searching the map for power stations, they were able to unlock the wildest GTA 6 secret I’ve seen so far.
I discovered this GTA 6 easter egg about 3 days ago, here it is in video form, I think I'm the first person to ever crack this code in the world so enjoy! #GTA6 pic.twitter.com/vTORjUlYNi
— Memeio (@MemeioYT) November 23, 2026
In that previously mentioned tower, Memeio discovered that same little sound secret, but also spotted a poster seemingly referencing a famous cheat code from the original Vice City on PC: “Life Is Passing Me By” which, in the original game, you could enter to speed up time. Memeio then explored the entire map and started to find various electrical substations that each seemed to be marked with letters from that cheat code. Eventually, they were able to figure out a series of switch and button puzzles spread across 12 spots in GTA 6. Memeio hit the buttons in a particular order to spell out the cheat code, which resulted in Memeio receiving a text message hinting at… something being available during specific hours at a power plant. They traveled to the spot at the right time and found a portal that teleported Jason back to the original Malibu Club, as seen in Vice City on PS2.
I’ll be honest; when I first saw people talking about this secret on social media, I dismissed it. It sounded too wild and impossible to be true. But then I remembered that tower with the Vice City noise, and so I decided to give it a shot. It took me about 30 minutes of flying around the map while following Memeio’s video guide to hit all the buttons. At one point I got in trouble with the cops, but thankfully, my dumpster lawyer let me hide in his office (the dumpster) to avoid them . GTA 6 is a weird game, folks.
Anyway, after hitting all the buttons at all the stations, I got the text message. I then headed to the power station within the correct time window, and to my surprise and delight, I found a big pink portal waiting for me behind a metal door. Opening the door activated a cutscene that teleported Jason back to the original Vice City, complete with stiff animations and Tommy’s famous blue Hawaiian shirt.
Here’s a video of me finding the portal and exploring the classic club:
There’s not much to see in the club. You can dance a bit, which is fun, and you can try to get a drink at the bar. However, because everyone in the old PS2-era GTA games had big blocky hands with no fingers, Jason can’t grab his wine and spills it.
After that, I headed up the back stairs and found Kent Paul (a character from the original Vice City ) hanging out and doing coke. Before I could chat with him, a new portal opened up and sucked me out of 2002 Vice City and back into 2026 Vice City. But I did get a nice gift: Tommy Vercetti’s iconic blue shirt, as well as a chopper motorcycle inspired by the American flag–painted bike you get early in GTA: Vice City.
I highly recommend you go hit these buttons and see this secret yourself, as it’s very impressive and is a real treat for longtime GTA fans. Now, I guess I’ll believe basically anything people claim is in this game because, at this point, it could be true.

A tech snafu at one of the world’s busiest airports on Sunday is delaying thousands of Delta Airlines flights headed ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
An issue with Delta Airlines’ weight and balance system at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is responsible for the delay at one of the busiest airports in the country, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement posted on social media.
More than 3,550 flights traveling within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed as of Sunday afternoon, according to Flight Aware .
The governmental agency urged travelers to check in with the airline for the latest information on their flights, and said that steps have already been taken to fix the issue.
“Delta is working to resolve issues with the airline’s weight and balance automation system,” the FAA statement said. “These delays are not related to any FAA air traffic systems.”
Delta said it is working limit congestion at its Atlanta hub.
“Delta teams are using manual workarounds to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” said Delta spokesperson Natalie Duggan. “We thank our customers for their patience and our people for their professionalism."
The issue on Sunday comes after a communications failure grounded all flights nationwide earlier this month, leading New York Gov. Kathy Hochul to call for the removal of U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
Other recent technological malfunctions have impacted other industries, including online banking systems and Microsoft Outlook.
Delta Airlines did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Gothamist.

Citi Bike members will soon pay less for electric bike rides under a new agreement between Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration and Lyft, which operates the bike-share program.
The deal will also freeze annual membership prices and other fees for members through May 2029.
Starting Jan. 19, 2027, Citi Bike members will pay no more than $3.65 for an e-bike ride lasting up to 45 minutes. The cap also applies to reduced-fare members and shorter rides that already cost less will remain at their current price.
Annual membership prices, member per-minute e-bike fees and charges for rides that exceed 45 minutes will be frozen at current rates until May 26, 2029, when Lyft’s contract with the city expires.
“Getting around New York City shouldn't come with a price tag that keeps climbing by the minute,” Mamdani wrote in a release announcing the agreement. “Because a more affordable city is one where getting around it doesn’t break the bank.”
Citi Bike members currently pay 27 cents per minute for e-bike rides, or $12.15 for a 45-minute ride, except for rides entering or leaving Manhattan, which are capped at $5.40. The annual membership fee is $239 and rides on regular bikes lasting up to 45 minutes are included.
Under the new agreement, members could save as much as $8.50 on a single e-bike ride, according to City Hall. The new cap replaces the existing $5.40 cap for rides entering or leaving Manhattan, as well as a one-time allotment of 60 e-bike minutes for members.
The agreement doesn't prohibit Lyft from increasing Citi Bike prices for non-members, who currently pay $4.99 for a ride up to 30 minutes on analog bikes and an additional 41 cents per-minute for e-bike rides.
The city has also agreed to help install electric charging infrastructure at more than 130 Citi Bike stations starting next year. This will allow the e-bikes to recharge while docked, rather than having Lyft workers swap out depleted batteries. City officials said the changes will reduce operating costs and make more e-bikes available to riders.
City Councilmember Lincoln Restler introduced a bill two years ago to rein in the rising cost of Citi Bike rides.
“ This is such a tremendous victory for Citi Bike riders,” Restler said. “The city had given Lyft a monopoly, essentially, with the Citi Bike program and the cost spiraled out of control in such a way where it felt like New Yorkers were being taken advantage of.”
Citi Bike raised prices six times from 2022 through January 2026, with Lyft recently blaming tariffs and inflation for the need to raise rates.
“We’re grateful to Mayor Mamdani and Commissioner Flynn for working with us to make Citi Bike an even more sustainable, reliable, and affordable option for New Yorkers,” Patrick Knoth, general manager of Citi Bike, wrote in a statement.
